hero-ride-loop.mp4.prompt:
Create a clean hand-drawn 2D skateboard-pushing animation cycle from this exact image. Camera and all background artwork remain perfectly static. Keep Zoomer, skateboard and cup in their exact original right-side screen position, preserving the open sunset sky on the left for website text. Preserve the original flat colors, crisp black outlines, face, orange hair, glasses, clothing, backpack, camo shoes, cup and board. No motion blur, ghosting, transparent doubles, morphing, 3D, zooms or cuts.

Animate ONE specific motion continuously for eight seconds: a calm repeating skateboard push cycle about every two seconds. The FRONT FOOT is the shoe already resting on the skateboard, at the RIGHT of the image. That shoe must remain completely planted at the same spot on the deck for every frame, with the sole always touching the deck. It never lifts, slides, changes shape or switches with the other foot. The REAR FOOT is the shoe that starts raised behind him, on the LEFT of his body. ONLY that rear foot moves: swing down beside the board, contact the pavement, push backward against the pavement, lift behind the body, then swing forward through the air and repeat. Clear foot-ground contact, a small supporting-knee bend and gentle torso balance. This is skateboarding, with one foot always fixed on the deck; never walking, running, hopping or swapping feet. The board itself remains stable in the exact same position; wheels rotate.

Both arms hold the ORIGINAL pose throughout: the cup stays upright at the original height in the original single hand, while the free arm stays down behind the hip. No arm swing across the body, no reaching for the drink, no grip changes, no sipping, waving or looking around. Two arms, two legs, one rider. The rhythmic rear-leg push repeats naturally at least four times from the very first frame through the final frame without any pause, glide hold, stop, final pose or reset. Movement is already ongoing at the beginning and continues beyond the end. Silent.
